title: Queues and deques
objective: Use first in, first out, and a double-ended queue, to find the maximum of every window.

sources.title: Laaksonen, Competitive Programmer's Handbook: sliding window minimum (the same method for the maximum)

simplifies: A plain queue only removes from the front. This uses a deque, which removes from both ends; both ends are O(1) in Python's deque.

quiz.prompt: Why drop smaller values from the back when a bigger one arrives?

options.text: They can never be a window's maximum while that bigger, newer value is in the window
options.explanation: Right. The newer value stays at least as long and beats them, so they are useless.
It saves memory too, but the reason is that they can no longer be an answer.
Nothing is sorted; the deque just keeps useful candidates.

quiz.prompt: In what order does a queue serve items?

options.explanation: Right. Like a line at a counter.
That is a priority queue (heap), covered later.
